reasoning: Failure-driven edits (Group 1) are kept in full. They add the verify-by-substitution step, the container-vs-member rule, the shared-base-name and middle-initial format rules, and the grammatical-number rule. All their targets exist in the current skill and none touch the protected section. All ten success-driven edits are kept because they cover patterns the failure edits do not address, and their anchors exist. Three adjustments avoid collisions. (1) The success 'group by description' insert shared an anchor with the failure VERIFY insert, so I moved it to the end of Rule 2 (after the 'Honor qualifiers' bullet). (2) The success rule to drop middle initials could contradict the failure rule that a clue-given middle name becomes 'First M. Last'. I added an explicit exception so the failure rule wins. (3) The success 'CATEGORY | clue | answer' replace and the verbatim 'What is/Who is' insert do not overlap with any failure edit, so they pass through unchanged.

edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
edits.content: - VERIFY before answering: substitute your candidate into the clue and check every descriptor, role, verb and date is true of it. A name that dominates the passages is often only the context figure (e.g. the sitting president), not the answer. 'Former first lady announced candidacy' -> the person who WAS a first lady and ran (Imelda Marcos), not the president whose name fills the pages. 'Admitted to the U.N. in 1971' -> the country admitted (China), not the one that lost its seat (Taiwan). Look for the sentence that lists candidates ('candidates, including former First Lady ...') or places the clue's distinctive phrase next to one entity ('Hostess Cupcakes ... split in half' -> cupcake), and prefer that entity over a more frequently mentioned one.

edits.target: Other named entities in the clue are anchors, never the answer.
edits.content: - Container vs member: when the clue says "this state's / this country's / this city's X includes A, B & C" or lists parts, branches or divisions, the listed items are anchors. Answer the whole that owns them ('Divisions of this state's national forest include Long Cane, Enoree & Tiger' -> the state, 'South Carolina'), never one of the listed members.

edits.target: do not append that role word to the answer.
edits.content:
- If the clue describes the SAME person or character under different epithets, roles or film titles ('In '84 he's a destroyer, in '82 just a barbarian'), the answer is the shared base name ('Conan'), not a title or phrase that includes the clue's epithets ('Conan the Destroyer' is wrong).
- If the clue gives a person's middle name ('His middle name was Gamaliel'), answer in the standard 'First M. Last' form with the middle name reduced to its initial ('Warren G. Harding'), not spelled out.

edits.target: - Use the singular form for a generic single object ('Well', not 'wells'), but keep the plural for crops, commodities and mass categories ('Bananas') or when the clue says 'these'/'ones'.
edits.content: - Match the grammatical number of the clue's noun. Use the singular for a generic single object ('Well', not 'wells'). Use the plural when the clue noun is plural ('canvas-covered blades of a windmill' -> 'Sails'; 'these', 'ones', 'muscles', 'group of ...'), and for crops, commodities and mass categories ('Bananas'). If a verbatim archive/flashcard hit shows the answer in a particular number, copy that number ('SAILS' -> 'Sails').

edits.target: The context passages about the topic usually reveal the link.
edits.content:
- A clue that is only a work's title, often with a year (e.g. '"Rachel, Rachel"(1968)'), asks for the work's creator: the director of a film, the author of a book, the composer of a piece. Pick the person that most passages pair with the title ('directed by X', 'novel by X'). Do not answer with the title itself or a plot detail.
- Terse 'YEAR: Starring/By/Written by PERSON' fragments (e.g. '1968:Starring Barbra Streisand') ask for the work (film, book, song, album) tied to BOTH the year and the person. Answer with the title that recurs across the passages with those two details, never the person named in the clue. This holds even if a crossword-style page hides its answer.
- A fragment such as '...as the U.S. holiday Decoration Day' or '...also known as X' is the tail of a sentence about an alias or former name. Answer with the other name that the passages tie to X ('originally called Decoration Day' -> 'Memorial Day').

edits.target: Before the answer tags, briefly quote the matched line.
edits.content: - An answer printed as a Jeopardy-style response ('The clue: ... "What is France?"', 'Who is Jesse Owens?') counts as a verbatim hit. Copy only the entity and drop 'What is' / 'Who is'. This applies even when the snippet comes from a news or game-show recap rather than an archive page. Treat only the contestant's WRONG responses as noise.

edits.target: - Otherwise, build the answer from passages that match several of the clue's details.
edits.content:
- Passage titles and headwords are strong evidence. When several passages whose titles or first lines echo the clue's details are all about one entity ('Shilling (British coin) - Wikipedia', 'Earl Warren - Wikipedia', 'Love Story (novel)'), that entity is the answer. Drop the parenthetical disambiguator and any ' - Wikipedia' suffix from the answer.
- If the clue contains a unique number, statistic, year or superlative ('1.7 people per square kilometer', 'banned in Boston in 1927'), search the passages for that same figure and take the entity stated next to it. Check it against the clue's other descriptors ('Central Asian' -> Mongolia). Passages are often noisy search results, so ignore off-topic ones and trust the few that repeat the clue's specifics.

edits.target: - Archive lines may also be formatted 'CATEGORY | clue text | answer'. Take the answer that follows the clue, even if the whole context is one short passage.
edits.content: - Archive lines may also be formatted 'CATEGORY | clue text | answer' (e.g. 'DALLAS | In 1985 he was run down... | Bobby Ewing. right: ...'). The first segment is only the category header (it is never the answer, even if it matches a clue word). Take the text that follows the clue, even if the whole context is one short passage.

edits.target: Do not talk yourself out of a well-supported entity.
edits.content: - If the clue appears verbatim in a snippet with no answer visible (a J! Archive page or a Jeopardy question dump cut off after the clue), that only confirms which clue is being asked. Take the answer from the other passages that repeat the clue's distinctive details, and answer confidently from them.

edits.target: - If the context offers several candidates (a different player in the same article, a film and its song), pick the one that satisfies ALL distinctive details: exact numbers, team, years, place. Do not choose one that fits only some.
edits.content: - Use any form hints in the clue as a final check on the candidate: '3-word phrase' (count the words), 'this largest ...', 'late', a stated decade or year, or a letter count in parentheses. If the candidate violates a hint, pick another.

edits.target: For people, prefer the form used in a verbatim answer from the context (Rule 3); otherwise use the name form most natural for the clue.
edits.content: - For people without a verbatim archive answer, use the common first + last name (e.g. 'Alan Shepard', not 'Alan B. Shepard, Jr.'). Drop middle initials, suffixes (Jr., III), honorifics and job titles, unless a single name is the standard form ('Madonna'), the passages' answer line uses a longer form, or the clue itself gives the person's middle name (then use 'First M. Last' as described below).

edits.target: Still apply the person-name rule above.
edits.content: - Name-change clues ('His name, pre-Muhammad Ali', 'formerly known as', 'born as'): give the earlier name in the short form that recurs most in the passages ('Cassius Clay'). Do not give the full legal name with middle names or suffixes ('Cassius Marcellus Clay Jr.'), and do not give a brief transitional name ('Cassius X').

edits.target: - Honor qualifiers when the context offers several names for the same thing: 'Greek god of erotic love' -> 'Eros' (not Roman 'Cupid').
edits.content: - When the clue defines a group by description ('these people born between '46 & '64', 'these fish'), answer with the common name for that group as the passages phrase it ('baby boomers'), not the date range or an example member.

edits.target: - Clue lists its own options ('Of North Park, East Park, West Park or South Park, it's where...'): the answer is exactly one of the listed options, copied verbatim. Use the context to pick which.
edits.content: - Numeric option lists ('Of 2, 5 or 10, the number of eyes on a bee'): find the passage that states the count for the exact subject. Add up the parts it lists (2 compound + 3 simple eyes = 5) and answer with the listed option equal to that total. Pick a single option and do not explain.
